key_insight: A discrete adjoint formulation inherits GSIS acceleration to efficiently compute optimization gradients across rarefied and continuum gas flows.
engineering_relevance: The method supports gradient-based design of thermal protection geometries and gas-delivery systems while balancing competing performance objectives.
method: Express kinetic and macroscopic GSIS equations as a coupled fixed-point system.
Derive coupled adjoint equations from a discrete Lagrangian containing both residual sets.
Alternate kinetic and macroscopic adjoint updates using established discrete adjoint techniques.
evidence_signal: NACA0012 sensitivities closely matched central finite differences, both primal and adjoint solvers converged within tens of iterations, and optimization reduced capsule peak heat flux by 6.54–14.17% and wafer-pressure variation from 1.49% to 0.06%.
watch_item: Implementation requires consistent differentiation of coupled kinetic and macroscopic residuals; the abstract does not establish performance beyond the reported test cases.
paper_title: Discrete adjoint method for the general synthetic iterative scheme for optimization of rarefied and continuum gas flows
